name: Continuity Scenes (character-locked, live-paced)
description: First-person / POV video where the SAME character (or set) appears across every scene, and scenes are rendered sequentially so each one flows from the last — giving a continuous, almost-live feel. You drop in a character sheet; the LLM picks an establishing scene from it, then every following scene references the previous render (and/or the sheet) so the look stays consistent. Pacing is driven by the audio: you set a per-episode min/max scene length (e.g. 1–10s or 5–20s) and the planner cuts more often where the narration is busy. Pipeline: idea → first-person script → audio → per-chapter subtitles → stitched timeline → Character Sheet (drop in the anchor) → Scene Plan (paced cuts) → sequential Continuity Render → Scene Review (approve) → Timestamp Video Assembly. Great for 'if I had $1000 today, here's how I'd multiply it' / 'if I had a MacBook today, here's how I'd make money with it' style POV advice — but the technique applies to any topic that benefits from a consistent on-screen character. SLOW by design (each scene waits on the previous render) in exchange for character consistency. NOT for evenly-distributed scene-images storytelling (use Narrative) and NOT for stock-footage (use Voice over Stock Footage).

idea.systemPromptRole: You are helping generate first-person, point-of-view episode ideas for a creator-led channel where one consistent on-screen character carries the whole video. Each idea should be framed from the creator's perspective and lend itself to a sequence of concrete, visualizable moments the character moves through (sitting at a desk, opening a laptop, walking into a shop, counting cash). Favour aspirational, actionable, 'here's exactly what I'd do' angles over abstract commentary.
idea.audienceDefault: viewers who want a relatable, first-person walkthrough they can imagine themselves doing
idea.guidanceText: Each idea should imply a clear sequence of scenes the character physically moves through, so the continuity chain has distinct beats to render. 'How to save money' is too abstract; 'If I had $1000 today, here's exactly what I'd do to multiply it' gives a walkable, scene-by-scene arc. Keep it first-person and concrete.

exampleIdeas.title: If I had $1000 today, here's exactly what I'd do to multiply it
exampleIdeas.logline: A first-person play-by-play: from an empty account to a working plan, each step shown as its own scene with the same person on screen.

exampleIdeas.title: If I had a MacBook today, here's how I'd make money with it
exampleIdeas.logline: One creator, one laptop — walking through the exact tools and first moves, scene by scene, to go from zero to first dollar.

script.systemPromptRole: You are writing a point-of-view narration where ONE character carries the whole video and the visuals are rendered scene-by-scene to match the audio. The narrative person (first / second / third) is set by the script's Point-of-view picker — follow it exactly. Write in a natural spoken voice. Crucially, give the visual planner clear, concrete physical beats to latch onto — what the on-screen character is doing, holding, looking at, or where they are — because each beat becomes its own rendered scene in a continuity chain. Short, vivid, action-anchored sentences beat long abstract ones.
additionalRules: Keep the chosen point of view (the Point-of-view setting) consistent throughout.
Anchor each idea to a concrete, visualizable action or location — the planner turns these into scenes.
Prefer short, punchy sentences over long abstract ones; busy passages should imply faster cuts.
Keep one consistent on-screen persona — don't introduce new unnamed people the chain can't render consistently.
Close with a clear payoff or call to action that lands the POV premise.
pacingArc: Hook: state the first-person premise ('If I had X today…')
Setup: the starting situation, shown as an establishing scene
Core: the step-by-step plan, each step its own concrete beat
Momentum: a busier stretch of quick actions (faster cuts)
Payoff: the result, tie back to the opening premise
script.closingHint: End on the payoff that resolves the opening 'if I had…' premise.

narratorStyles.label: Casual first-person
narratorStyles.description: Relaxed, conversational 'talking to a friend' voice. The default for POV creator content.

narratorStyles.label: High-energy hustle
narratorStyles.description: Faster, punchier, motivational — leans into momentum and quick wins.

narratorStyles.label: Calm and deliberate
narratorStyles.description: Measured, confident, 'let me walk you through this' pacing. Good for thoughtful walkthroughs.

imagePrompts.purposeNote: (populated by the Scene Plan page — the LLM produces one visual prompt per planned scene, paced to the user-set min/max scene length. The Continuity Render then generates each scene sequentially, anchoring on the character sheet and optionally referencing the previous scene's render.)
imagePrompts.visualStyleHint: Keep the SAME character, wardrobe, and setting consistent across every scene — the continuity chain depends on it. Describe what the character is doing in this beat; the look is carried by the reference images.
imagePrompts.defaultStyleTag: Consistent character, consistent lighting and style across scenes. Cohesive, grounded, slightly cinematic. The same person should be recognizable in every frame.

thumbnail.conceptGuidance: A cover featuring the story's recurring character as a clear hero, mid-action in a relatable setting, in the same consistent look used across the chain. Authentic and energetic — the viewer should recognize the character instantly.
compositionRules: Recurring character as the clear hero, large in frame, mid-action
Consistent wardrobe and style with the rest of the chain
Relatable, grounded setting with a clean area for the title
